+from pathlib import Path
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+import requests, bs4, sys, json, concurrent.futures
+
+out = Path('editorial/research/google-merchant-center-image-requirements')
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+sources = {
+ 'main': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en',
+ 'small': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en',
+ 'additional': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en',
+ 'lifestyle': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en',
+ 'best-practices': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en',
+ 'automatic': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en',
+ 'overlay': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en',
+ 'apparel': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en',
+ 'big': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en',
+ 'status': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en',
+ 'trained': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia',
+ 'composite': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic',
+ 'algorithmic': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia',
+}
+phase = sys.argv[1]
+def capture(item):
+ name,url=item
+ response=requests.get(url, timeout=45)
+ response.raise_for_status()
+ soup=bs4.BeautifulSoup(response.text,'html.parser')
+ main=soup.select_one('article') or soup.select_one('main') or soup.body
+ for node in main.select('script,style,nav,footer'): node.decompose()
+ # Exclude unrelated product promotion, retaining all specification sections.
+ for node in list(main.select('p,li,div.note')):
+  if 'Product Studio' in node.get_text() and node.parent:
+   if 'metadata' not in node.get_text() and 'meta data' not in node.get_text(): node.decompose()
+ text=main.get_text('\n',strip=True).replace('\u2014',' - ')
+ text=text.replace('Product Studio','[unrelated tool example omitted]')
+ header=f'Source: {url}\nCaptured: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}\nHTTP: {response.status_code}\nPublication date: not displayed on Google Help; see IPTC concept timestamps where present.\nCapture method: HTML article text; unrelated tool promotion omitted; long dashes normalized.\n\n'
+ (out/f'{phase}-{name}.txt').write_text(header+text+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
+ return {'source':name,'http':response.status_code,'chars':len(text)}
+with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as pool:
+ for result in pool.map(capture,sources.items()): print(json.dumps(result))

+ inventory.push({file:`${name}-2026-10-23.png`,url,selector,captured:new Date().toISOString()});
+ console.log(name+' captured');
+}
+writeFileSync(`${dir}/screenshots.json`,JSON.stringify(inventory,null,2)+'\n');
+await browser.close();

+title: Google Merchant Center Image Requirements 2026

+<!-- HERO SECTION -->
+
+# Google Shopping image requirements for 2026
+
+Reviewed October 23, 2026. By Cyril Drouin.
+
+Merchant Center checks the picture and the file behind its URL. Choose the
+right image attribute, distinguish today’s minimum from the coming change,
+and preserve the metadata on AI-generated files.
+
+<!-- INTRODUCTION -->
+
+## What are the Google Shopping image requirements?
+
+Google Shopping image requirements cover the pictured product, file size,
+and crawlable URL. Prepare main images at Google’s recommended 1500 x 1500
+pixels or above, keep AI metadata, and check the dated minimums below.
+Lifestyle images have their own rules. hubStudio supplies image creation
+and export; you submit the URLs through your Merchant Center data source.
+
+### Main image: image_link
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Required image | Main view of the item being sold | Image link |
+| Current minimum | 100 x 100 px non-clothing; 250 x 250 px clothing | Image too small |
+| From January 31, 2027 | 500 x 500 px for all products | Image too small |
+| Recommended size | Around 1500 x 1500 px or above | Image link |
+| Maximum | 64 megapixels; 16 MB | Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Image link |
+| Background | Solid white or light neutral recommended; clear staged images also acceptable | Image best practices |
+
+> Google recommends around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above for the main image.
+> Its attribute table lists a ceiling of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Method:
+> direct reading of the published formatting specifications.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image link, undated, accessed October
+> 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+Keep exports below both ceilings. The Image too big help page uses stricter
+wording in its headline than in its body, so there’s little reason to build
+an export exactly on either boundary. File weight and pixel count need
+separate checks.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too big, undated, accessed October
+23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Minimum-size transition -->
+
+## When does the new minimum image size apply?
+
+Google’s attribute table already prints the incoming minimum. Its dedicated
+Image too small page explains the transition:
+
+> “Enforcement of the new requirements will begin January 31, 2027.” The new
+> general minimum is 500 x 500 pixels. Until then, the stated floors remain
+> 100 x 100 for non-clothing and 250 x 250 for clothing. Warnings began in
+> July 2026. Method: read the dated transition notice alongside the temporary
+> requirements on the same page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too small, undated, accessed
+> October 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en
+
+The page gives an enforcement date but no dated announcement. For new main
+images, use the incoming minimum as your production floor. YouTube Shopping ads on TV already
+require 500 x 500 pixels. Lifestyle images have a higher attribute-specific
+minimum, below.
+
+A main image below the applicable minimum can cause product disapproval.
+Open Products, then Needs attention, and use the upcoming-enforcement
+warnings to find affected products. Check the file at the submitted URL:
+a small thumbnail can fail even when a larger master exists elsewhere.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Additional images -->
+
+## What belongs in additional_image_link?
+
+Use additional images for another angle, a close-up, or the product in use.
+They inherit the main image’s technical requirements, but Google permits
+staging and views that show only part of the product. An image of one
+component can also explain a bundle.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 10 additional images; optional | Additional image link |
+| Minimum | Main-image size requirements, including the dated transition above | Additional image link |
+| Recommended size | 1500 x 1500 px or above | Additional image link |
+| Maximum | Same as main: 64 MP and 16 MB | Additional image link; Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Additional image link |
+| Background | Staging and product-in-use scenes allowed | Additional image link |
+
+> Google allows up to 10 additional images and recommends 1500 x 1500 pixels
+> or above. Method: read the attribute’s format table, notice, and exceptions
+> together, including its rule for undersized additional images.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+There’s a useful distinction in that last rule: an additional image below
+the minimum won’t be shown, but it does not itself disapprove the product.
+That exception is about size, not permission to add promotional overlays.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Lifestyle images -->
+
+## How does lifestyle_image_link differ?
+
+This optional attribute supplies a scene for free listings: the product in
+use, staged in a room, or shown as part of a set. It is not a replacement for
+the required main image.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 5 lifestyle images | Lifestyle image link |
+| Minimum | 600 x 600 px on the attribute-specific page | Lifestyle image link |
+| Recommended size | Highest-resolution full-size image available, within the caps | Lifestyle image link |
+| Maximum | 64 MP and 16 MB | Lifestyle image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Lifestyle image link |
+| Background | Real-world or staged context; no borders or padding | Lifestyle image link |
+
+> The lifestyle attribute permits up to 5 images, requires at least 600 x 600
+> pixels, and gives upper limits of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Its aspect-ratio
+> range is printed as “2:0 and 2:3”; the first value is unusable. Method:
+> direct reading of the attribute page, with that defect left uncorrected.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Lifestyle image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en
+
+Google’s general Image best practices page says lifestyle images follow
+primary-image resolution guidelines. The specific attribute page still
+requires 600 x 600. Follow that higher minimum. No verified replacement for
+the malformed aspect ratio is supplied here; check the intended crop in
+Merchant Center before preparing the full set.
+
+Source for the general guidance: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best
+practices, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Disapprovals -->
+
+## What gets a Merchant Center image rejected?
+
+Start with the issue named in Needs attention. A compliant composition can
+still fail because Google cannot fetch the file.
+
+| Problem | What to change | Google Help source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Added sale text, shipping claims, or a watermark | Supply a product image without the promotional layer | Text on image |
+| A border, placeholder, or unrelated item in the main image | Show the actual item sold; keep unrelated props out of the main view | Image link |
+| Wrong color or pattern | Match the pictured variant to the product and landing page | Clothing and accessories |
+| Broken or blocked URL | Serve the actual supported image file at a public, crawlable URL | Product image status |
+| File extension and format disagree | Fix the export and URL so they identify the same format | Product image status |
+
+Branding printed on the physical product is different from a logo added over
+the photograph. Google permits the former. Its rules also contain specific
+generic-image exceptions for hardware, vehicle parts, and software; a
+placeholder is not automatically acceptable for other categories. A set sold
+together can appear together; unrelated products are the problem in a main
+image. AI disclosure labels have a separate exception, explained below.
+
+Sources: Google Merchant Center Help, Text on image and Image link,
+undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+For URL failures, test the exact submitted address outside a signed-in
+session. Confirm that Googlebot and Googlebot-Image can fetch it. Fixing the
+picture won’t repair an inaccessible server path.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, How to check and manage your product
+image status, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Framing and variants -->
+
+## Do backgrounds, apparel, and variants need separate treatment?
+
+A white background is recommended, not universally mandatory. Google’s
+Image best practices page accepts staged images that clearly show the item.
+Its clothing guide recommends showing clothing on a model, while shoes,
+bags, and accessories appear alone in main images and on a model in
+additional views. For a full-body clothing photo, keep the head and feet.
+
+> Google recommends a product filling 75 to 90 percent of the frame. This is
+> framing guidance, not a published width-versus-area measurement formula.
+> Method: read the recommendation in the Image best practices page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best practices, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+Check the variant, too. The clothing guide says both main and additional
+images should show the variant being sold, with the correct option selected
+on the destination page. A neat photograph of the wrong finish is still
+the wrong photograph.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Best practices for advertising clothing
+and accessories, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en
+
+Use the white background packshot guide for production. The Platform specs
+hub, Amazon product image requirements, and Shopify product image sizes
+cover other destinations. The Shopify platform page explains the store
+workflow; its image settings do not replace Merchant Center’s feed rules.
+
+<!-- SECTION: AI metadata -->
+
+## Can AI-generated product images keep their required metadata?
+
+Google allows AI-generated imagery subject to its image rules and requires
+metadata identifying that origin. Preserve the embedded IPTC
+DigitalSourceType property through export and delivery.
+
+> “Don't remove embedded metadata tags” is Google’s instruction for images
+> created with generative AI. Method: direct reading of the additional-image
+> attribute’s metadata rule, also present on the main and lifestyle pages.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+IPTC’s identifier trainedAlgorithmicMedia describes content created with a
+trained generative model. compositeSynthetic describes a composite with
+generative elements, such as a photographed product in an AI-made setting.
+algorithmicMedia covers a different process: algorithmic creation without
+a model trained on sampled content. They are not interchangeable labels.
+
+Source: IPTC NewsCodes, Digital Source Type vocabulary, checked October 23,
+2026. https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia
+
+The Image studio supports output up to 4K, depending on the engine. Its
+transparent-background option is limited to the ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines
+with PNG or WebP. The free Image editor can crop the result. These are
+production tools, not a Merchant Center connection.
+
+> hubStudio’s help center documents output up to 4K and limits transparent
+> output to its ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines in PNG or WebP. Method: checked
+> against the current Image studio help and the binding product description.
+> Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image, checked October 23, 2026.
+> https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/create-an-image
+
+Choose Download image for the original render. Do not use Download clean
+copy or an Image anonymizer export for a feed: they strip the embedded
+markers. Inspect the final file after any crop, conversion, or compression;
+downloading the original is not proof that every required tag is present.
+If tags are missing, correct the metadata before submission, then inspect the
+file served at the final image URL. The eCommerce
+design service covers work made with the studio team inside the app.
+
+Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image and Assets Library and the tools,
+checked October 23, 2026. https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/assets-library
+
+<!-- SECTION: Automatic improvements -->
+
+## Will automatic image improvements fix a disapproval?
+
+They may fix an overlay. Google says automatic image improvements are off
+by default; enable them under Products, Automations. Merchant Center then
+tries to remove detected text, watermarks, or logos. Successful changes can
+replace the image and restore approval. Inspect the result in Needs
+attention, where affected products show the original and improved images.
+
+Google also exempts AI disclosure labels from its overlay and watermark
+prohibitions. Do not treat that exception as permission to add a sale badge,
+or as a substitute for the embedded metadata rule. This is production
+practice, not legal advice.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Allow Merchant Center to improve your
+product images, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: FAQ -->
+
+## FAQ
+
+### What size should Google Shopping images be?
+
+Use Google’s recommendation of around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above as the
+starting point for main and additional images. Check both pixel count and
+file weight before delivery. The minimum is a separate question: the table
+above distinguishes the temporary floors, the incoming general floor, and
+the lifestyle-specific requirement.
+
+### Why was my Google Merchant Center image disapproved?
+
+Read the issue in Products, Needs attention. It may concern promotional
+overlays, an undersized image, the wrong product, or a file Google cannot
+reach. Test the submitted URL before commissioning another image. If the
+problem is an overlay, replace the image or review the result of automatic
+image improvements.
+
+### Can I use AI-generated images in Google Shopping?
+
+Yes, if they meet the image rules and contain metadata identifying their
+AI origin. Preserve the embedded DigitalSourceType property, and inspect
+the delivered file after editing or conversion. Also compare the visible
+product with the actual item: a correctly tagged image can still depict
+the wrong color, shape, or variant.
+
+### What is the minimum image size for Google Merchant Center in 2027?
+
+The general minimum becomes 500 x 500 pixels on January 31, 2027. Prepare
+replacement main images before that date. Do not apply that number to every
+attribute without checking: the lifestyle page specifies a higher floor,
+and TV Shopping ads already have their own requirement. The dated table
+above keeps those cases separate.
+
+### Do Google Shopping images need a white background?
+
+Not universally. Google recommends solid white or light-neutral backgrounds
+for main images and also accepts staged images that clearly show the
+product. Lifestyle images serve a different purpose: context or use.
+Keep that distinction when preparing the set, and don’t add promotional
+text simply because an image has a lifestyle setting.
+
+### What is a lifestyle image in Merchant Center?
+
+It shows the product in a setting or in use and is submitted through the
+optional lifestyle_image_link attribute for free listings. It does not
+replace the main image. The attribute’s own page sets a higher minimum
+resolution than the general incoming rule and prohibits borders, padding,
+promotional elements, and other text.
+

+## R7. Gate
+
+Every planned factual claim is primary or explicitly cut. The documented
+conflicts can be explained without guessing a value. Research file written
+before the article. The source brief is amended for those distinctions.

+Performed after drafting in createarticle iteration 8; the completed audit is
+recorded below when that iteration runs.

+from pathlib import Path
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+import requests, bs4, sys, json, concurrent.futures
+
+out = Path('editorial/research/google-merchant-center-image-requirements')
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+sources = {
+ 'main': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en',
+ 'small': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en',
+ 'additional': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en',
+ 'lifestyle': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en',
+ 'best-practices': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en',
+ 'automatic': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en',
+ 'overlay': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en',
+ 'apparel': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en',
+ 'big': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en',
+ 'status': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en',
+ 'trained': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia',
+ 'composite': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic',
+ 'algorithmic': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia',
+}
+phase = sys.argv[1]
+def capture(item):
+ name,url=item
+ response=requests.get(url, timeout=45)
+ response.raise_for_status()
+ soup=bs4.BeautifulSoup(response.text,'html.parser')
+ main=soup.select_one('article') or soup.select_one('main') or soup.body
+ for node in main.select('script,style,nav,footer'): node.decompose()
+ # Exclude unrelated product promotion, retaining all specification sections.
+ for node in list(main.select('p,li,div.note')):
+  if 'Product Studio' in node.get_text() and node.parent:
+   if 'metadata' not in node.get_text() and 'meta data' not in node.get_text(): node.decompose()
+ text=main.get_text('\n',strip=True).replace('\u2014',' - ')
+ text=text.replace('Product Studio','[unrelated tool example omitted]')
+ header=f'Source: {url}\nCaptured: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}\nHTTP: {response.status_code}\nPublication date: not displayed on Google Help; see IPTC concept timestamps where present.\nCapture method: HTML article text; unrelated tool promotion omitted; long dashes normalized.\n\n'
+ (out/f'{phase}-{name}.txt').write_text(header+text+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
+ return {'source':name,'http':response.status_code,'chars':len(text)}
+with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as pool:
+ for result in pool.map(capture,sources.items()): print(json.dumps(result))

+---
+title: Google Merchant Center Image Requirements 2026
+slug: google-merchant-center-image-requirements
+description: Google Shopping image rules per attribute: sizes, file caps, formats, what gets disapproved, the 500 px minimum from January 2027 and the AI image rule.
+excerpt: Match each product image to its feed attribute, prepare for the new minimum size, and keep AI metadata through the final export.
+template: spec
+---
+
+<!-- HERO SECTION -->
+
+# Google Shopping image requirements for 2026
+
+Reviewed October 23, 2026. By Cyril Drouin.
+
+Merchant Center checks the picture and the file behind its URL. Choose the
+right image attribute, distinguish today’s minimum from the coming change,
+and preserve the metadata on AI-generated files.
+
+<!-- INTRODUCTION -->
+
+## What are the Google Shopping image requirements?
+
+Google Shopping image requirements cover the pictured product, file size,
+and crawlable URL. Prepare main images at Google’s recommended 1500 x 1500
+pixels or above, keep AI metadata, and check the dated minimums below.
+Lifestyle images have their own rules. hubStudio supplies image creation
+and export; you submit the URLs through your Merchant Center data source.
+
+### Main image: image_link
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Required image | Main view of the item being sold | Image link |
+| Current minimum | 100 x 100 px non-clothing; 250 x 250 px clothing | Image too small |
+| From January 31, 2027 | 500 x 500 px for all products | Image too small |
+| Recommended size | Around 1500 x 1500 px or above | Image link |
+| Maximum | 64 megapixels; 16 MB | Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Image link |
+| Background | Solid white or light neutral recommended; clear staged images also acceptable | Image best practices |
+
+> Google recommends around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above for the main image.
+> Its attribute table lists a ceiling of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Method:
+> direct reading of the published formatting specifications.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image link, undated, accessed October
+> 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+Keep exports below both ceilings. The Image too big help page uses stricter
+wording in its headline than in its body, so there’s little reason to build
+an export exactly on either boundary. File weight and pixel count need
+separate checks.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too big, undated, accessed October
+23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Minimum-size transition -->
+
+## When does the new minimum image size apply?
+
+Google’s attribute table already prints the incoming minimum. Its dedicated
+Image too small page explains the transition:
+
+> “Enforcement of the new requirements will begin January 31, 2027.” The new
+> general minimum is 500 x 500 pixels. Until then, the stated floors remain
+> 100 x 100 for non-clothing and 250 x 250 for clothing. Warnings began in
+> July 2026. Method: read the dated transition notice alongside the temporary
+> requirements on the same page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too small, undated, accessed
+> October 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en
+
+The page gives an enforcement date but no dated announcement. For new main
+images, use the incoming minimum as your production floor. YouTube Shopping ads on TV already
+require 500 x 500 pixels. Lifestyle images have a higher attribute-specific
+minimum, below.
+
+A main image below the applicable minimum can cause product disapproval.
+Open Products, then Needs attention, and use the upcoming-enforcement
+warnings to find affected products. Check the file at the submitted URL:
+a small thumbnail can fail even when a larger master exists elsewhere.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Additional images -->
+
+## What belongs in additional_image_link?
+
+Use additional images for another angle, a close-up, or the product in use.
+They inherit the main image’s technical requirements, but Google permits
+staging and views that show only part of the product. An image of one
+component can also explain a bundle.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 10 additional images; optional | Additional image link |
+| Minimum | Main-image size requirements, including the dated transition above | Additional image link |
+| Recommended size | 1500 x 1500 px or above | Additional image link |
+| Maximum | Same as main: 64 MP and 16 MB | Additional image link; Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Additional image link |
+| Background | Staging and product-in-use scenes allowed | Additional image link |
+
+> Google allows up to 10 additional images and recommends 1500 x 1500 pixels
+> or above. Method: read the attribute’s format table, notice, and exceptions
+> together, including its rule for undersized additional images.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+An additional image below
+the minimum won’t be shown, but it does not itself disapprove the product.
+That exception is about size, not permission to add promotional overlays.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Lifestyle images -->
+
+## How does lifestyle_image_link differ?
+
+This optional attribute supplies a scene for free listings: the product in
+use, staged in a room, or shown as part of a set. It is not a replacement for
+the required main image.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 5 lifestyle images | Lifestyle image link |
+| Minimum | 600 x 600 px on the attribute-specific page | Lifestyle image link |
+| Recommended size | Highest-resolution full-size image available, within the caps | Lifestyle image link |
+| Maximum | 64 MP and 16 MB | Lifestyle image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Lifestyle image link |
+| Background | Real-world or staged context; no borders or padding | Lifestyle image link |
+
+> The lifestyle attribute permits up to 5 images, requires at least 600 x 600
+> pixels, and gives upper limits of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Its aspect-ratio
+> range is printed as “2:0 and 2:3”; the first value is unusable. Method:
+> direct reading of the attribute page, with that defect left uncorrected.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Lifestyle image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en
+
+Google’s general Image best practices page says lifestyle images follow
+primary-image resolution guidelines. The specific attribute page still
+requires 600 x 600. Follow that higher minimum. No verified replacement for
+the malformed aspect ratio is supplied here; check the intended crop in
+Merchant Center before preparing the full set.
+
+Source for the general guidance: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best
+practices, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Disapprovals -->
+
+## What gets a Merchant Center image rejected?
+
+Read the issue named in Needs attention before changing the artwork. Google
+may simply be unable to fetch the file.
+
+| Problem | What to change | Google Help source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Added sale text, shipping claims, or a watermark | Supply a product image without the promotional layer | Text on image |
+| A border, placeholder, or unrelated item in the main image | Show the actual item sold; keep unrelated props out of the main view | Image link |
+| Wrong color or pattern | Match the pictured variant to the product and landing page | Clothing and accessories |
+| Broken or blocked URL | Serve the actual supported image file at a public, crawlable URL | Product image status |
+| File extension and format disagree | Fix the export and URL so they identify the same format | Product image status |
+
+Branding printed on the physical product is different from a logo added over
+the photograph. Google permits the former. Its rules also contain specific
+generic-image exceptions for hardware, vehicle parts, and software; a
+placeholder is not automatically acceptable for other categories. A set sold
+together can appear together; unrelated products are the problem in a main
+image. AI disclosure labels have a separate exception, explained below.
+
+Sources: Google Merchant Center Help, Text on image and Image link,
+undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+For URL failures, test the exact submitted address outside a signed-in
+session. Confirm that Googlebot and Googlebot-Image can fetch it. Fixing the
+picture won’t repair an inaccessible server path.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, How to check and manage your product
+image status, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Framing and variants -->
+
+## Do backgrounds, apparel, and variants need separate treatment?
+
+A white background is recommended, not universally mandatory. Google’s
+Image best practices page accepts staged images that clearly show the item.
+Its clothing guide recommends showing clothing on a model, while shoes,
+bags, and accessories appear alone in main images and on a model in
+additional views. For a full-body clothing photo, keep the head and feet.
+
+> Google recommends a product filling 75 to 90 percent of the frame. This is
+> framing guidance, not a published width-versus-area measurement formula.
+> Method: read the recommendation in the Image best practices page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best practices, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+Check the variant, too. The clothing guide says both main and additional
+images should show the variant being sold, with the correct option selected
+on the destination page. Check those images against the selected option,
+especially when similar finishes share a folder.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Best practices for advertising clothing
+and accessories, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en
+
+Use the white background packshot guide for production. The Platform specs
+hub, Amazon product image requirements, and Shopify product image sizes
+cover other destinations. The Shopify platform page explains the store
+workflow; its image settings do not replace Merchant Center’s feed rules.
+
+<!-- SECTION: AI metadata -->
+
+## Can AI-generated product images keep their required metadata?
+
+Google allows AI-generated imagery subject to its image rules and requires
+metadata identifying that origin. Preserve the embedded IPTC
+DigitalSourceType property through export and delivery.
+
+> “Don't remove embedded metadata tags” is Google’s instruction for images
+> created with generative AI. Method: direct reading of the additional-image
+> attribute’s metadata rule, also present on the main and lifestyle pages.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+IPTC’s identifier trainedAlgorithmicMedia describes content created with a
+trained generative model. compositeSynthetic describes a composite with
+generative elements, such as a photographed product in an AI-made setting.
+algorithmicMedia covers a different process: algorithmic creation without
+a model trained on sampled content. They are not interchangeable labels.
+
+Source: IPTC NewsCodes, Digital Source Type vocabulary, checked October 23,
+2026. https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia
+
+The Image studio supports output up to 4K, depending on the engine. Its
+transparent-background option is limited to the ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines
+with PNG or WebP. The free Image editor can crop the result. These are
+production tools, not a Merchant Center connection.
+
+> hubStudio’s help center documents output up to 4K and limits transparent
+> output to its ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines in PNG or WebP. Method: checked
+> against the current Image studio help and the binding product description.
+> Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image, checked October 23, 2026.
+> https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/create-an-image
+
+Choose Download image for the original render. Do not use Download clean
+copy or an Image anonymizer export for a feed: they strip the embedded
+markers. Inspect the final file after any crop, conversion, or compression;
+downloading the original is not proof that every required tag is present.
+If tags are missing, correct the metadata before submission, then inspect the
+file served at the final image URL. The eCommerce
+design service covers work made with the studio team inside the app.
+
+Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image and Assets Library and the tools,
+checked October 23, 2026. https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/assets-library
+
+<!-- SECTION: Automatic improvements -->
+
+## Will automatic image improvements fix a disapproval?
+
+They may fix an overlay. Google says automatic image improvements are off
+by default; enable them under Products, Automations. Merchant Center then
+tries to remove detected text, watermarks, or logos. Successful changes can
+replace the image and restore approval. Inspect the result in Needs
+attention, where affected products show the original and improved images.
+
+Google also exempts AI disclosure labels from its overlay and watermark
+prohibitions. Do not treat that exception as permission to add a sale badge,
+or as a substitute for the embedded metadata rule. This is production
+practice, not legal advice.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Allow Merchant Center to improve your
+product images, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: FAQ -->
+
+## FAQ
+
+### What size should Google Shopping images be?
+
+Use Google’s recommendation of around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above as the
+starting point for main and additional images. Check both pixel count and
+file weight before delivery. The minimum is a separate question: the table
+above distinguishes the temporary floors, the incoming general floor, and
+the lifestyle-specific requirement.
+
+### Why was my Google Merchant Center image disapproved?
+
+Read the issue in Products, Needs attention. It may concern promotional
+overlays, an undersized image, the wrong product, or a file Google cannot
+reach. Test the submitted URL before commissioning another image. If the
+problem is an overlay, replace the image or review the result of automatic
+image improvements.
+
+### Can I use AI-generated images in Google Shopping?
+
+Yes, if they meet the image rules and contain metadata identifying their
+AI origin. Preserve the embedded DigitalSourceType property, and inspect
+the delivered file after editing or conversion. Also compare the visible
+product with the actual item: a correctly tagged image can still depict
+the wrong color, shape, or variant.
+
+### What is the minimum image size for Google Merchant Center in 2027?
+
+The general minimum becomes 500 x 500 pixels on January 31, 2027. Prepare
+replacement main images before that date. Do not apply that number to every
+attribute without checking: the lifestyle page specifies a higher floor,
+and TV Shopping ads already have their own requirement. The dated table
+above keeps those cases separate.
+
+### Do Google Shopping images need a white background?
+
+Not universally. Google recommends solid white or light-neutral backgrounds
+for main images and also accepts staged images that clearly show the
+product. Lifestyle images serve a different purpose: context or use.
+Keep that distinction when preparing the set, and don’t add promotional
+text simply because an image has a lifestyle setting.
+
+### What is a lifestyle image in Merchant Center?
+
+It shows the product in a setting or in use and is submitted through the
+optional lifestyle_image_link attribute for free listings. It does not
+replace the main image. The attribute’s own page sets a higher minimum
+resolution than the general incoming rule and prohibits borders, padding,
+promotional elements, and other text.
+

+from pathlib import Path

+import requests, bs4, sys, json, concurrent.futures

+out = Path('editorial/research/google-merchant-center-image-requirements')
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+sources = {
+ 'main': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en',
+ 'small': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en',
+ 'additional': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en',
+ 'lifestyle': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en',
+ 'best-practices': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en',
+ 'automatic': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en',
+ 'overlay': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en',
+ 'apparel': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en',
+ 'big': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en',
+ 'status': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en',
+ 'trained': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia',
+ 'composite': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic',
+ 'algorithmic': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia',
+}
+phase = sys.argv[1]
+def capture(item):
+ name,url=item
+ response=requests.get(url, timeout=45)
+ response.raise_for_status()
+ soup=bs4.BeautifulSoup(response.text,'html.parser')
+ main=soup.select_one('article') or soup.select_one('main') or soup.body
+ for node in main.select('script,style,nav,footer'): node.decompose()
+ # Exclude unrelated product promotion, retaining all specification sections.
+ for node in list(main.select('p,li,div.note')):
+  if 'Product Studio' in node.get_text() and node.parent:
+   if 'metadata' not in node.get_text() and 'meta data' not in node.get_text(): node.decompose()
+ text=main.get_text('\n',strip=True).replace('\u2014',' - ')
+ text=text.replace('Product Studio','[unrelated tool example omitted]')
+ header=f'Source: {url}\nCaptured: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}\nHTTP: {response.status_code}\nPublication date: not displayed on Google Help; see IPTC concept timestamps where present.\nCapture method: HTML article text; unrelated tool promotion omitted; long dashes normalized.\n\n'
+ (out/f'{phase}-{name}.txt').write_text(header+text+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
+ return {'source':name,'http':response.status_code,'chars':len(text)}
+with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as pool:
+ for result in pool.map(capture,sources.items()): print(json.dumps(result))

+---
+title: Google Merchant Center Image Requirements 2026
+slug: google-merchant-center-image-requirements
+description: Google Shopping image rules per attribute: sizes, file caps, formats, what gets disapproved, the 500 px minimum from January 2027 and the AI image rule.
+excerpt: Match each product image to its feed attribute, prepare for the new minimum size, and keep AI metadata through the final export.
+template: spec
+---
+
+<!-- HERO SECTION -->
+
+# Google Shopping image requirements for 2026
+
+Reviewed October 23, 2026. By Cyril Drouin.
+
+Merchant Center checks the picture and the file behind its URL. Choose the
+right image attribute, distinguish today’s minimum from the coming change,
+and preserve the metadata on AI-generated files.
+
+<!-- INTRODUCTION -->
+
+## What are the Google Shopping image requirements?
+
+Google Shopping image requirements cover the pictured product, file size,
+and crawlable URL. Prepare main images at Google’s recommended 1500 x 1500
+pixels or above, keep AI metadata, and check the dated minimums below.
+Lifestyle images have their own rules. hubStudio supplies image creation
+and export; you submit the URLs through your Merchant Center data source.
+
+### Main image: image_link
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Required image | Main view of the item being sold | Image link |
+| Current minimum | 100 x 100 px non-clothing; 250 x 250 px clothing | Image too small |
+| From January 31, 2027 | 500 x 500 px for all products | Image too small |
+| Recommended size | Around 1500 x 1500 px or above | Image link |
+| Maximum | 64 megapixels; 16 MB | Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Image link |
+| Background | Solid white or light neutral recommended; clear staged images also acceptable | Image best practices |
+
+> Google recommends around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above for the main image.
+> Its attribute table lists a ceiling of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Method:
+> direct reading of the published formatting specifications.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image link, undated, accessed October
+> 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+Keep exports below both ceilings. The Image too big help page uses stricter
+wording in its headline than in its body, so there’s little reason to build
+an export exactly on either boundary. File weight and pixel count need
+separate checks.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too big, undated, accessed October
+23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Minimum-size transition -->
+
+## When does the new minimum image size apply?
+
+Google’s attribute table already prints the incoming minimum. Its dedicated
+Image too small page explains the transition:
+
+> “Enforcement of the new requirements will begin January 31, 2027.” The new
+> general minimum is 500 x 500 pixels. Until then, the stated floors remain
+> 100 x 100 for non-clothing and 250 x 250 for clothing. Warnings began in
+> July 2026. Method: read the dated transition notice alongside the temporary
+> requirements on the same page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too small, undated, accessed
+> October 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en
+
+The page gives an enforcement date but no dated announcement. For new main
+images, use the incoming minimum as your production floor. YouTube Shopping ads on TV already
+require 500 x 500 pixels. Lifestyle images have a higher attribute-specific
+minimum, below.
+
+A main image below the applicable minimum can cause product disapproval.
+Open Products, then Needs attention, and use the upcoming-enforcement
+warnings to find affected products. Check the file at the submitted URL:
+a small thumbnail can fail even when a larger master exists elsewhere.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Additional images -->
+
+## What belongs in additional_image_link?
+
+Use additional images for another angle, a close-up, or the product in use.
+They inherit the main image’s technical requirements, but Google permits
+staging and views that show only part of the product. An image of one
+component can also explain a bundle.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 10 additional images; optional | Additional image link |
+| Minimum | Main-image size requirements, including the dated transition above | Additional image link |
+| Recommended size | 1500 x 1500 px or above | Additional image link |
+| Maximum | Same as main: 64 MP and 16 MB | Additional image link; Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Additional image link |
+| Background | Staging and product-in-use scenes allowed | Additional image link |
+
+> Google allows up to 10 additional images and recommends 1500 x 1500 pixels
+> or above. Method: read the attribute’s format table, notice, and exceptions
+> together, including its rule for undersized additional images.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+An additional image below
+the minimum won’t be shown, but it does not itself disapprove the product.
+That exception is about size, not permission to add promotional overlays.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Lifestyle images -->
+
+## How does lifestyle_image_link differ?
+
+This optional attribute supplies a scene for free listings: the product in
+use, staged in a room, or shown as part of a set. It is not a replacement for
+the required main image.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 5 lifestyle images | Lifestyle image link |
+| Minimum | 600 x 600 px on the attribute-specific page | Lifestyle image link |
+| Recommended size | Highest-resolution full-size image available, within the caps | Lifestyle image link |
+| Maximum | 64 MP and 16 MB | Lifestyle image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Lifestyle image link |
+| Background | Real-world or staged context; no borders or padding | Lifestyle image link |
+
+> The lifestyle attribute permits up to 5 images, requires at least 600 x 600
+> pixels, and gives upper limits of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Its aspect-ratio
+> range is printed as “2:0 and 2:3”; the first value is unusable. Method:
+> direct reading of the attribute page, with that defect left uncorrected.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Lifestyle image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en
+
+Google’s general Image best practices page says lifestyle images follow
+primary-image resolution guidelines. The specific attribute page still
+requires 600 x 600. Follow that higher minimum. No verified replacement for
+the malformed aspect ratio is supplied here; check the intended crop in
+Merchant Center before preparing the full set.
+
+Source for the general guidance: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best
+practices, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Disapprovals -->
+
+## What gets a Merchant Center image rejected?
+
+Read the issue named in Needs attention before changing the artwork. Google
+may simply be unable to fetch the file.
+
+| Problem | What to change | Google Help source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Added sale text, shipping claims, or a watermark | Supply a product image without the promotional layer | Text on image |
+| A border, placeholder, or unrelated item in the main image | Show the actual item sold; keep unrelated props out of the main view | Image link |
+| Wrong color or pattern | Match the pictured variant to the product and landing page | Clothing and accessories |
+| Broken or blocked URL | Serve the actual supported image file at a public, crawlable URL | Product image status |
+| File extension and format disagree | Fix the export and URL so they identify the same format | Product image status |
+
+Branding printed on the physical product is different from a logo added over
+the photograph. Google permits the former. Its rules also contain specific
+generic-image exceptions for hardware, vehicle parts, and software; a
+placeholder is not automatically acceptable for other categories. A set sold
+together can appear together; unrelated products are the problem in a main
+image. AI disclosure labels have a separate exception, explained below.
+
+Sources: Google Merchant Center Help, Text on image and Image link,
+undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+For URL failures, test the exact submitted address outside a signed-in
+session. Confirm that Googlebot and Googlebot-Image can fetch it. Fixing the
+picture won’t repair an inaccessible server path.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, How to check and manage your product
+image status, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Framing and variants -->
+
+## Do backgrounds, apparel, and variants need separate treatment?
+
+A white background is recommended, not universally mandatory. Google’s
+Image best practices page accepts staged images that clearly show the item.
+Its clothing guide recommends showing clothing on a model, while shoes,
+bags, and accessories appear alone in main images and on a model in
+additional views. For a full-body clothing photo, keep the head and feet.
+
+> Google recommends a product filling 75 to 90 percent of the frame. This is
+> framing guidance, not a published width-versus-area measurement formula.
+> Method: read the recommendation in the Image best practices page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best practices, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+Check the variant, too. The clothing guide says both main and additional
+images should show the variant being sold, with the correct option selected
+on the destination page. Check those images against the selected option,
+especially when similar finishes share a folder.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Best practices for advertising clothing
+and accessories, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en
+
+Use the white background packshot guide for production. The Platform specs
+hub, Amazon product image requirements, and Shopify product image sizes
+cover other destinations. The Shopify platform page explains the store
+workflow; its image settings do not replace Merchant Center’s feed rules.
+
+<!-- SECTION: AI metadata -->
+
+## Can AI-generated product images keep their required metadata?
+
+Google allows AI-generated imagery subject to its image rules and requires
+metadata identifying that origin. Preserve the embedded IPTC
+DigitalSourceType property through export and delivery.
+
+> “Don’t remove embedded metadata tags” is Google’s instruction for images
+> created with generative AI. Method: direct reading of the additional-image
+> attribute’s metadata rule, also present on the main and lifestyle pages.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+IPTC’s identifier trainedAlgorithmicMedia describes content created with a
+trained generative model. compositeSynthetic describes a composite with
+generative elements, such as a photographed product in an AI-made setting.
+algorithmicMedia covers a different process: algorithmic creation without
+a model trained on sampled content. They are not interchangeable labels.
+
+Source: IPTC NewsCodes, Digital Source Type vocabulary, checked October 23,
+2026. https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia
+
+The Image studio supports output up to 4K, depending on the engine. Its
+transparent-background option is limited to the ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines
+with PNG or WebP. The free Image editor can crop the result. These are
+production tools, not a Merchant Center connection.
+
+> hubStudio’s help center documents output up to 4K and limits transparent
+> output to its ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines in PNG or WebP. Method: checked
+> against the current Image studio help and the binding product description.
+> Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image, checked October 23, 2026.
+> https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/create-an-image
+
+Choose Download image for the original render. Do not use Download clean
+copy or an Image anonymizer export for a feed: they strip the embedded
+markers. Inspect the final file after any crop, conversion, or compression;
+downloading the original is not proof that every required tag is present.
+If tags are missing, correct the metadata before submission, then inspect the
+file served at the final image URL. The eCommerce
+design service covers work made with the studio team inside the app.
+
+Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image and Assets Library and the tools,
+checked October 23, 2026. https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/assets-library
+
+<!-- SECTION: Automatic improvements -->
+
+## Will automatic image improvements fix a disapproval?
+
+They may fix an overlay. Google says automatic image improvements are off
+by default; enable them under Products, Automations. Merchant Center then
+tries to remove detected text, watermarks, or logos. Successful changes can
+replace the image and restore approval. Inspect the result in Needs
+attention, where affected products show the original and improved images.
+
+Google also exempts AI disclosure labels from its overlay and watermark
+prohibitions. Do not treat that exception as permission to add a sale badge,
+or as a substitute for the embedded metadata rule. This is production
+practice, not legal advice.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Allow Merchant Center to improve your
+product images, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: FAQ -->
+
+## FAQ
+
+### What size should Google Shopping images be?
+
+Use Google’s recommendation of around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above as the
+starting point for main and additional images. Check both pixel count and
+file weight before delivery. The minimum is a separate question: the table
+above distinguishes the temporary floors, the incoming general floor, and
+the lifestyle-specific requirement.
+
+### Why was my Google Merchant Center image disapproved?
+
+Read the issue in Products, Needs attention. It may concern promotional
+overlays, an undersized image, the wrong product, or a file Google cannot
+reach. Test the submitted URL before commissioning another image. If the
+problem is an overlay, replace the image or review the result of automatic
+image improvements.
+
+### Can I use AI-generated images in Google Shopping?
+
+Yes, if they meet the image rules and contain metadata identifying their
+AI origin. Preserve the embedded DigitalSourceType property, and inspect
+the delivered file after editing or conversion. Also compare the visible
+product with the actual item: a correctly tagged image can still depict
+the wrong color, shape, or variant.
+
+### What is the minimum image size for Google Merchant Center in 2027?
+
+The general minimum becomes 500 x 500 pixels on January 31, 2027. Prepare
+replacement main images before that date. Do not apply that number to every
+attribute without checking: the lifestyle page specifies a higher floor,
+and TV Shopping ads already have their own requirement. The dated table
+above keeps those cases separate.
+
+### Do Google Shopping images need a white background?
+
+Not universally. Google recommends solid white or light-neutral backgrounds
+for main images and also accepts staged images that clearly show the
+product. Lifestyle images serve a different purpose: context or use.
+Keep that distinction when preparing the set, and don’t add promotional
+text simply because an image has a lifestyle setting.
+
+### What is a lifestyle image in Merchant Center?
+
+It shows the product in a setting or in use and is submitted through the
+optional lifestyle_image_link attribute for free listings. It does not
+replace the main image. The attribute’s own page sets a higher minimum
+resolution than the general incoming rule and prohibits borders, padding,
+promotional elements, and other text.

+from pathlib import Path
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+import requests, bs4, sys, json, concurrent.futures
+
+out = Path('editorial/research/google-merchant-center-image-requirements')
+out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+sources = {
+ 'main': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en',
+ 'small': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en',
+ 'additional': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en',
+ 'lifestyle': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en',
+ 'best-practices': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en',
+ 'automatic': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en',
+ 'overlay': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en',
+ 'apparel': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en',
+ 'big': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en',
+ 'status': 'https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en',
+ 'trained': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia',
+ 'composite': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic',
+ 'algorithmic': 'https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia',
+}
+phase = sys.argv[1]
+def capture(item):
+ name,url=item
+ response=requests.get(url, timeout=45)
+ response.raise_for_status()
+ soup=bs4.BeautifulSoup(response.text,'html.parser')
+ main=soup.select_one('article') or soup.select_one('main') or soup.body
+ for node in main.select('script,style,nav,footer'): node.decompose()
+ # Exclude unrelated product promotion, retaining all specification sections.
+ for node in list(main.select('p,li,div.note')):
+  if 'Product Studio' in node.get_text() and node.parent:
+   if 'metadata' not in node.get_text() and 'meta data' not in node.get_text(): node.decompose()
+ text=main.get_text('\n',strip=True).replace('\u2014',' - ')
+ text=text.replace('Product Studio','[unrelated tool example omitted]')
+ header=f'Source: {url}\nCaptured: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}\nHTTP: {response.status_code}\nPublication date: not displayed on Google Help; see IPTC concept timestamps where present.\nCapture method: HTML article text; unrelated tool promotion omitted; long dashes normalized.\n\n'
+ (out/f'{phase}-{name}.txt').write_text(header+text+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
+ return {'source':name,'http':response.status_code,'chars':len(text)}
+with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as pool:
+ for result in pool.map(capture,sources.items()): print(json.dumps(result))

+---
+title: Google Merchant Center Image Requirements 2026
+slug: google-merchant-center-image-requirements
+description: Google Shopping image rules per attribute: sizes, file caps, formats, what gets disapproved, the 500 px minimum from January 2027 and the AI image rule.
+excerpt: Match each product image to its feed attribute, prepare for the new minimum size, and keep AI metadata through the final export.

+---
+
+<!-- HERO SECTION -->
+
+# Google Shopping image requirements for 2026
+
+Reviewed October 23, 2026. By Cyril Drouin.
+
+Merchant Center checks the picture and the file behind its URL. The image
+attribute determines which rules apply. Today’s minimum and the coming
+minimum are different, and AI metadata must survive the export.
+
+<!-- INTRODUCTION -->
+
+## What are the Google Shopping image requirements?
+
+Google Shopping image requirements cover the pictured product, file size,
+and crawlable URL. Prepare main images at Google’s recommended 1500 x 1500
+pixels or above, keep AI metadata, and check the dated minimums below.
+Lifestyle images have their own rules. hubStudio supplies image creation
+and export; you submit the URLs through your Merchant Center data source.
+
+### Main image: image_link
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Required image | Main view of the item being sold | Image link |
+| Current minimum | 100 x 100 px non-clothing; 250 x 250 px clothing | Image too small |
+| From January 31, 2027 | 500 x 500 px for all products | Image too small |
+| Recommended size | Around 1500 x 1500 px or above | Image link |
+| Maximum | 64 megapixels; 16 MB | Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Image link |
+| Background | Solid white or light neutral recommended; clear staged images also acceptable | Image best practices |
+
+> Google recommends around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above for the main image.
+> Its attribute table lists a ceiling of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Method:
+> direct reading of the published formatting specifications.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image link, undated, accessed October
+> 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+Keep exports below both ceilings. The Image too big help page uses stricter
+wording in its headline than in its body, so there’s little reason to build
+an export exactly on either boundary.
+
+Check both file weight and pixel count.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too big, undated, accessed October
+23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12473903?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Minimum-size transition -->
+
+## When does the new minimum image size apply?
+
+Google’s attribute table already prints the incoming minimum. Its dedicated
+Image too small page explains the transition:
+
+> “Enforcement of the new requirements will begin January 31, 2027.” The new
+> general minimum is 500 x 500 pixels. Until then, the stated floors remain
+> 100 x 100 for non-clothing and 250 x 250 for clothing. Warnings began in
+> July 2026. Method: read the dated transition notice alongside the temporary
+> requirements on the same page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image too small, undated, accessed
+> October 23, 2026. https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159030?hl=en
+
+The page gives an enforcement date but no dated announcement. For new main
+images, use the incoming minimum as your production floor. YouTube Shopping ads on TV already
+require 500 x 500 pixels. Lifestyle images have a higher attribute-specific
+minimum, below.
+
+A main image below the applicable minimum can cause product disapproval.
+Open Products, then Needs attention, and use the upcoming-enforcement
+warnings to find affected products. Check the file at the submitted URL:
+a small thumbnail can fail even when a larger master exists elsewhere.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Additional images -->
+
+## What belongs in additional_image_link?
+
+An additional image can show the reverse side. A close-up may explain a
+detail that disappears in the main view; a wider shot can show the item in use.
+They inherit the main image’s technical requirements, but Google permits
+staging and views that show only part of the product. An image of one
+component can also explain a bundle.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 10 additional images; optional | Additional image link |
+| Minimum | Main-image size requirements, including the dated transition above | Additional image link |
+| Recommended size | 1500 x 1500 px or above | Additional image link |
+| Maximum | Same as main: 64 MP and 16 MB | Additional image link; Image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Additional image link |
+| Background | Staging and product-in-use scenes allowed | Additional image link |
+
+> Google allows up to 10 additional images and recommends 1500 x 1500 pixels
+> or above. Method: read the attribute’s format table, notice, and exceptions
+> together, including its rule for undersized additional images.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+An additional image below
+the minimum won’t be shown, but it does not itself disapprove the product.
+That exception is about size, not permission to add promotional overlays.
+
+<!-- SECTION: Lifestyle images -->
+
+## How does lifestyle_image_link differ?
+
+This optional attribute supplies a scene for free listings: the product in
+use, staged in a room, or shown as part of a set. It is not a replacement for
+the required main image.
+
+| Check | Specification | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Number | Up to 5 lifestyle images | Lifestyle image link |
+| Minimum | 600 x 600 px on the attribute-specific page | Lifestyle image link |
+| Recommended size | Highest-resolution full-size image available, within the caps | Lifestyle image link |
+| Maximum | 64 MP and 16 MB | Lifestyle image link |
+| Formats | JPEG, WebP, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF | Lifestyle image link |
+| Background | Real-world or staged context; no borders or padding | Lifestyle image link |
+
+> The lifestyle attribute permits up to 5 images, requires at least 600 x 600
+> pixels, and gives upper limits of 64 megapixels and 16 MB. Its aspect-ratio
+> range is printed as “2:0 and 2:3”; the first value is unusable. Method:
+> direct reading of the attribute page, with that defect left uncorrected.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Lifestyle image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9103186?hl=en
+
+Google’s general Image best practices page says lifestyle images follow
+primary-image resolution guidelines. The specific attribute page still
+requires 600 x 600. Follow that higher minimum. No verified replacement for
+the malformed aspect ratio is supplied here; check the intended crop in
+Merchant Center before preparing the full set.
+
+Source for the general guidance: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best
+practices, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Disapprovals -->
+
+## What gets a Merchant Center image rejected?
+
+Read the issue named in Needs attention before changing the artwork. Google
+may simply be unable to fetch the file.
+
+| Problem | What to change | Google Help source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Added sale text, shipping claims, or a watermark | Supply a product image without the promotional layer | Text on image |
+| A border, placeholder, or unrelated item in the main image | Show the actual item sold; keep unrelated props out of the main view | Image link |
+| Wrong color or pattern | Match the pictured variant to the product and landing page | Clothing and accessories |
+| Broken or blocked URL | Serve the actual supported image file at a public, crawlable URL | Product image status |
+| File extension and format disagree | Fix the export and URL so they identify the same format | Product image status |
+
+Branding printed on the physical product is different from a logo added over
+the photograph. Google permits the former. Its rules also contain specific
+generic-image exceptions for hardware, vehicle parts, and software; a
+placeholder is not automatically acceptable for other categories. A set sold
+together can appear together; unrelated products are the problem in a main
+image. AI disclosure labels have a separate exception, explained below.
+
+Sources: Google Merchant Center Help, Text on image and Image link,
+undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12158684?hl=en
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324350?hl=en
+
+For URL failures, test the exact submitted address outside a signed-in
+session. Confirm that Googlebot and Googlebot-Image can fetch it. Fixing the
+picture won’t repair an inaccessible server path.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, How to check and manage your product
+image status, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353079?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: Framing and variants -->
+
+## Do backgrounds, apparel, and variants need separate treatment?
+
+A white background is recommended, not universally mandatory. Google’s
+Image best practices page accepts staged images that clearly show the item.
+Its clothing guide recommends showing clothing on a model, while shoes,
+bags, and accessories appear alone in main images and on a model in
+additional views. For a full-body clothing photo, keep the head and feet.
+
+> Google recommends a product filling 75 to 90 percent of the frame. This is
+> framing guidance, not a published width-versus-area measurement formula.
+> Method: read the recommendation in the Image best practices page.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Image best practices, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/18353357?hl=en
+
+Check the variant, too. The clothing guide says both main and additional
+images should show the variant being sold, with the correct option selected
+on the destination page. Check those images against the selected option,
+especially when similar finishes share a folder.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Best practices for advertising clothing
+and accessories, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7348545?hl=en
+
+Use the white background packshot guide for production. The Platform specs
+hub, Amazon product image requirements, and Shopify product image sizes
+cover other destinations. The Shopify platform page explains the store
+workflow; its image settings do not replace Merchant Center’s feed rules.
+
+<!-- SECTION: AI metadata -->
+
+## Can AI-generated product images keep their required metadata?
+
+Google allows AI-generated imagery subject to its image rules and requires
+metadata identifying that origin. Preserve the embedded IPTC
+DigitalSourceType property through export and delivery.
+
+> “Don’t remove embedded metadata tags” is Google’s instruction for images
+> created with generative AI. Method: direct reading of the additional-image
+> attribute’s metadata rule, also present on the main and lifestyle pages.
+> Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Additional image link, undated,
+> accessed October 23, 2026.
+> https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324370?hl=en
+
+IPTC’s identifier trainedAlgorithmicMedia describes content created with a
+trained generative model. compositeSynthetic describes a composite with
+generative elements, such as a photographed product in an AI-made setting.
+algorithmicMedia covers a different process: algorithmic creation without
+a model trained on sampled content. They are not interchangeable labels.
+
+Source: IPTC NewsCodes, Digital Source Type vocabulary, checked October 23,
+2026. https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicMedia
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/compositeSynthetic
+https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/algorithmicMedia
+
+The Image studio supports output up to 4K, depending on the engine. Its
+transparent-background option is limited to the ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines
+with PNG or WebP. The free Image editor can crop the result. These are
+production tools, not a Merchant Center connection.
+
+> hubStudio’s help center documents output up to 4K and limits transparent
+> output to its ChatGPT Image 2.5 engines in PNG or WebP. Method: checked
+> against the current Image studio help and the binding product description.
+> Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image, checked October 23, 2026.
+> https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/create-an-image
+
+Choose Download image for the original render.
+
+Do not use Download clean
+copy or an Image anonymizer export for a feed: they strip the embedded
+markers. Inspect the final file after any crop, conversion, or compression;
+downloading the original is not proof that every required tag is present.
+If tags are missing, correct the metadata before submission, then inspect the
+file served at the final image URL. The eCommerce
+design service covers work made with the studio team inside the app.
+
+Source: hubStudio Help, Create an image and Assets Library and the tools,
+checked October 23, 2026. https://www.hubstudio.ai/help/assets-library
+
+<!-- SECTION: Automatic improvements -->
+
+## Will automatic image improvements fix a disapproval?
+
+They may fix an overlay. Google says automatic image improvements are off
+by default; enable them under Products, Automations. Merchant Center then
+tries to remove detected text, watermarks, or logos. Successful changes can
+replace the image and restore approval. Inspect the result in Needs
+attention, where affected products show the original and improved images.
+
+Google also exempts AI disclosure labels from its overlay and watermark
+prohibitions. Do not treat that exception as permission to add a sale badge,
+or as a substitute for the embedded metadata rule. This is production
+practice, not legal advice.
+
+Source: Google Merchant Center Help, Allow Merchant Center to improve your
+product images, undated, accessed October 23, 2026.
+https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12724659?hl=en
+
+<!-- SECTION: FAQ -->
+
+## FAQ
+
+### What size should Google Shopping images be?
+
+Use Google’s recommendation of around 1500 x 1500 pixels or above as the
+starting point for main and additional images. Check both pixel count and
+file weight before delivery. The minimum is a separate question: the table
+above distinguishes the temporary floors, the incoming general floor, and
+the lifestyle-specific requirement.
+
+### Why was my Google Merchant Center image disapproved?
+
+Read the issue in Products, Needs attention. It may concern promotional
+overlays, an undersized image, the wrong product, or a file Google cannot
+reach. Test the submitted URL before commissioning another image. If the
+problem is an overlay, replace the image or review the result of automatic
+image improvements.
+
+### Can I use AI-generated images in Google Shopping?
+
+Yes, if they meet the image rules and contain metadata identifying their
+AI origin. Preserve the embedded DigitalSourceType property, and inspect
+the delivered file after editing or conversion. Also compare the visible
+product with the actual item: a correctly tagged image can still depict
+the wrong color, shape, or variant.
+
+### What is the minimum image size for Google Merchant Center in 2027?
+
+The general minimum becomes 500 x 500 pixels on January 31, 2027. Prepare
+replacement main images before that date. Do not apply that number to every
+attribute without checking: the lifestyle page specifies a higher floor,
+and TV Shopping ads already have their own requirement. The dated table
+above keeps those cases separate.
+
+### Do Google Shopping images need a white background?
+
+Not universally. Google recommends solid white or light-neutral backgrounds
+for main images and also accepts staged images that clearly show the
+product. Lifestyle images serve a different purpose: context or use.
+Keep that distinction when preparing the set, and don’t add promotional
+text simply because an image has a lifestyle setting.
+
+### What is a lifestyle image in Merchant Center?
+
+It shows the product in a setting or in use and is submitted through the
+optional lifestyle_image_link attribute for free listings. It does not
+replace the main image. The attribute’s own page sets a higher minimum
+resolution than the general incoming rule and prohibits borders, padding,
+promotional elements, and other text.
+

+image improvements against their source pages.
